quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #23
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: If the rear of your car skids to the left, what should you do?

options.text: Steer to the right.
Steer to the left.
Tap your brakes lightly and shift into neutral.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer to the left.
questions.explanation: When your car skids, take your foot off the brake and steer in the direction you want to go. If the rear skids left, steer left. This brings the front and rear into line and straightens the car.

questions.question: How can you avoid hydroplaning when driving in rain?

options.text: Drive at a speed appropriate for ideal conditions.
Apply your brakes as soon as your car starts to skid.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: When driving too fast in wet conditions, your tires can lose contact with the road. The car rides on water instead of gripping the road. This is hydroplaning. Driving slower in rain prevents this.

questions.question: If a tire blows out while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Apply the brake and hold it.
Hold the steering wheel tightly and use the brakes lightly.
Pull over quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel tightly and use the brakes lightly.
questions.explanation: If a tire blows out, hold the steering wheel tight and keep the car straight. Slow down gradually by releasing the gas and braking lightly. Pull off the road in a safe place instead of stopping on the road.

questions.question: Which road surface freezes first?

options.text: A tunnel
An intersection
A bridge

questions.correctAnswerText: A bridge
questions.explanation: Bridges freeze before other road surfaces and thaw after them. This happens because bridges are exposed to cold air from both above and below.

questions.question: In Kentucky, when can drivers use hand signals instead of mechanical turn signals?

options.text: If the vehicle is not equipped with mechanical turn signals.
If the driver prefers to use hand signals.
Never.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: In Kentucky, all cars must have working mechanical turn signals. Hand signals are not allowed for passenger vehicles. Farm vehicles, construction vehicles, animal-drawn vehicles, and bicycles are exceptions.

questions.question: How often should you check your rearview mirrors?

options.text: Often to see how traffic is moving behind you.
To see if a vehicle is in your blind spot.
Only when you are slowing down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Often to see how traffic is moving behind you.
questions.explanation: Check your rearview mirrors frequently while driving. This helps you know where other vehicles are near you.

questions.question: What do broken yellow lines mean?

options.text: Indicate no passing zones.
Separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction.
Separate lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Separate lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. Dashed yellow lines mean you can pass when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: When is it legal to turn left at a red light after stopping?

options.text: You are traveling on a two-way street and turning onto a two-way street.
You are traveling on a one-way street and turning onto another one-way street.
You yield to all other traffic at the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are traveling on a one-way street and turning onto another one-way street.
questions.explanation: After a complete stop, you may turn left at a red light only if you are on a one-way street turning onto another one-way street. Make sure there are no signs that say no left turn.

questions.question: Oncoming vehicles are to your left and parked vehicles are to your right. Where should you steer?

options.text: Closer to the oncoming vehicles than the parked vehicles.
Closer to the parked vehicles than the oncoming vehicles.
A middle course between the oncoming and parked vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: A middle course between the oncoming and parked vehicles.
questions.explanation: Steer in the middle between oncoming traffic and parked vehicles. This gives you the most space on both sides.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop sign ahead.
Railroad crossing ahead.
Construction ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossing ahead.
questions.explanation: A round sign always means a railroad crossing is ahead.

questions.question: When driving alongside another vehicle on a multilane road, you should:

options.text: Keep the same speed.
Ask the other driver to slow down.
Speed up or slow down to change position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up or slow down to change position.
questions.explanation: Do not drive directly beside other vehicles on multilane roads. The other driver may not see you and could hit your car when changing lanes. Move ahead or fall back to avoid their blind spot.

questions.question: A driver license is a:

options.text: Right.
Privilege.
Requirement.

questions.correctAnswerText: Privilege.
questions.explanation: A driver license is a privilege. You must earn and keep it. It is not a right.

questions.question: You may cross double yellow lines to pass another vehicle if:

options.text: The vehicle in front of you moves to the right.
The yellow line on your side is broken.
The yellow line on the opposite side is broken.

questions.correctAnswerText: The yellow line on your side is broken.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line on your side means you can pass if it is safe. A solid yellow line means you cannot pass.

questions.question: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, turn into:

options.text: Any lane.
The first lane.
The second lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The first lane.
questions.explanation: Always turn into the first available legal lane. When turning onto a one-way street, this means the first lane.

questions.question: At a flashing yellow light, you should:

options.text: Yield to all traffic before entering the intersection.
Stop, then enter when it is safe.
Slow down and proceed carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down and look before crossing. Proceed with caution.

questions.question: You are in a left turn lane with oncoming traffic. You should:

options.text: Move to the left of the center lane.
Signal about 100 feet before the intersection.
Turn your front wheels to the left to prepare.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal about 100 feet before the intersection.
questions.explanation: Always signal before you turn. Keep your wheels straight until it is safe to turn. This prevents another car from pushing you into oncoming traffic if it hits you from behind.

questions.question: Always stop before crossing railroad tracks when:

options.text: Your vehicle cannot completely cross the tracks before stopping.
The railroad crossing is in a city with frequent trains.
You are carrying young children.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your vehicle cannot completely cross the tracks before stopping.
questions.explanation: A train can come at any time. Make sure your car clears the tracks completely before you stop. Do not stop on the tracks.

questions.question: At a "Yield" sign, you must:

options.text: Yield to traffic that could cause a crash.
Yield only to vehicles on your right.
Always slow down but never stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to traffic that could cause a crash.
questions.explanation: At a yield sign, slow down or stop if needed. Give the right-of-way to any traffic close enough to cause a crash.

questions.question: At intersections, crosswalks, and railroad crossings, you should:

options.text: Stop, listen, and go slowly.
Look left and right to see what is coming.
Slowly pass vehicles stopped for no reason.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look left and right to see what is coming.
questions.explanation: Always look left and right when entering an area where people or other traffic may be crossing your path.

questions.question: Large trucks lose speed when:

options.text: Going up long or steep hills.
Going around long, gradual curves.
Going down long, gradual hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Going up long or steep hills.
questions.explanation: Large trucks slow down on hills because they accelerate slowly. Give trucks extra space on hills.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Intersection ahead.
Merging traffic.
Steep hill ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steep hill ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert drivers to possible dangers. This sign warns you that a steep hill is coming. Slow down to avoid crashes and brake damage.

questions.question: When is it most important to be careful when turning or stopping in rain?

options.text: After it has been raining all day.
One half hour after it stops raining.
During the first half hour of rain.

questions.correctAnswerText: During the first half hour of rain.
questions.explanation: Be extra careful during the first half hour of rain. Oil from cars has not yet washed off the road, creating a slippery mix with the rain.

questions.question: Adjust the driver's seat so you can see the pavement ____ in front of your vehicle.

options.text: 12 to 15 feet
12 to 15 inches
5 to 10 feet

questions.correctAnswerText: 12 to 15 feet
questions.explanation: Adjust the driver's seat so you can see the pavement 12 to 15 feet ahead. Your chest should be 10 to 12 inches from the steering wheel center. Your shoulders should be at or above the top of the steering wheel.

questions.question: What is the default speed limit in a business or residential area?

options.text: 15 mph.
25 mph.
35 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: 35 mph.
questions.explanation: In a business or residential area, the speed limit is 35 miles per hour unless a different speed limit is posted. Always follow posted speed limits.

questions.question: At an intersection where you cannot see clearly to the side, what should you do?

options.text: Slow down and look both ways.
Maintain your speed and look both ways.
Stop, then inch forward until you can see clearly in both directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, then inch forward until you can see clearly in both directions.
questions.explanation: Stop completely at the intersection. Then move forward slowly until you can see clearly in both directions before proceeding.

questions.question: Which statement is true about medications and driving?

options.text: Most cold medications can make a person drowsy.
Over-the-counter medications cannot harm driving ability if taken as directed.
Medications are always safe to take while driving if prescribed by a doctor.

questions.correctAnswerText: Most cold medications can make a person drowsy.
questions.explanation: All medications, prescription or over-the-counter, can be dangerous while driving. Cold and allergy medicines can make you drowsy and reduce your driving ability. Know how your medication affects you before driving.

questions.question: You are turning left at an upcoming intersection. Yield to:

options.text: Oncoming vehicles also turning left.
All approaching vehicles.
Pedestrians on the sidewalk waiting for a "Walk" signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: All approaching vehicles.
questions.explanation: When turning left, you must yield to all approaching pedestrians, bicyclists, and vehicles that have a green light.

questions.question: When should you not use your horn?

options.text: When visibility ahead is limited.
If you might hit another vehicle.
Near blind pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: Near blind pedestrians.
questions.explanation: Do not use your horn near blind pedestrians. It may confuse them or be dangerous. Yield to the pedestrian and proceed safely.

questions.question: What does a steady red arrow on a traffic light mean?

options.text: Drivers cannot turn in the indicated direction.
Drivers may turn in the indicated direction after coming to a complete stop.
Drivers may turn in the indicated direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers cannot turn in the indicated direction.
questions.explanation: A steady red arrow means do not proceed in that direction. Stop and wait for a green signal before turning.

questions.question: In bad weather, you should:

options.text: Steer off the road.
Drive in a low gear.
Steer and brake smoothly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer and brake smoothly.
questions.explanation: In bad weather, avoid sudden braking and sharp turns. These actions make your vehicle harder to control. Steer and brake gently instead.

questions.question: What does alcohol affect first?

options.text: Vision.
Judgment.
Balance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Judgment.
questions.explanation: Alcohol affects the parts of your brain that control judgment and skill first. It goes from your stomach into your blood, then spreads to the rest of your body. Alcohol reduces all the abilities you need to drive safely.

questions.question: When changing lanes, what should you do?

options.text: Rely on the rearview mirror.
Look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move.
Rely on the left side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move.
questions.explanation: Look over your shoulder to check for traffic in your blind spot. Check several times before changing lanes. Watch the traffic in front of you and next to you at the same time.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should never:

options.text: Cross the centerline in an intersection.
Check your blind spots by looking over your left or right shoulder.
Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cross the centerline in an intersection.
questions.explanation: Do not pass or change lanes in an intersection. Before changing lanes, look over your shoulder to check your blind spot and check for drivers trying to enter the same lane as you.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Hospital.
Upcoming intersection.
Railroad crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Upcoming intersection.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. This sign warns drivers that an intersection is coming up so they can prepare for traffic or prepare to turn.

questions.question: What color are regulatory signs?

options.text: Green.
Yellow.
White.

questions.correctAnswerText: White.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs tell drivers about specific laws they must follow. These signs are usually white squares or rectangles with black, red, or green letters or symbols. They cover rules about traffic direction, lane use, turning, speed, and parking.

questions.question: Alcohol in any amount is:

options.text: A stimulant.
A depressant.
Neither of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: A depressant.
questions.explanation: Alcohol is always a depressant. It slows down nerve impulses and body functions. This reduces self-control and harms concentration and alertness.

questions.question: When exiting the interstate, when should you start slowing down?

options.text: About halfway through the deceleration lane.
As you approach the deceleration lane.
Immediately upon entering the deceleration lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Immediately upon entering the deceleration lane.
questions.explanation: Keep your speed until you enter the deceleration lane. Then slow down to the speed posted for the exit ramp.

questions.question: When entering a freeway, how should you check traffic?

options.text: Using your rearview and side mirrors.
Using your rearview mirror.
Using your side mirror and looking over your shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using your side mirror and looking over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Use your side mirror and look over your shoulder to see traffic when entering a freeway. This helps you see and expect what other drivers are doing.

questions.question: What lane must you be in to make a left turn from a one-way street?

options.text: The lane nearest the left curb.
The lane nearest the center of the street.
The lane nearest the right curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane nearest the left curb.
questions.explanation: Turn from the lane closest to where you want to go, into the first available legal lane. For a left turn from a one-way street, use the lane nearest the left curb.

questions.question: When you see a stop sign, what should you do?

options.text: Check for vehicles only in the direction you plan to go, then proceed.
Let all vehicles that arrive before or after you go first.
Check for traffic in all directions before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check for traffic in all directions before proceeding.
questions.explanation: Come to a full stop at the sign. Check for traffic in all directions before you go.
